summary: Paul Horn was an Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistics scholar. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and earned his PhD at the University of Halle under Christian Bartholomae, later serving as a professor at the University of Strasbourg.

Paul Horsch studied Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies at Fribourg, Paris (PhD under Bloch, Lacombe, and Renou), Cambridge, Lausanne, and Marburg under Nobel. He taught at Visva-Bharati (1952–1956) and the University of Zurich (PD 1959, professor 1967–1971).

Paul J. Griffiths studied Buddhist studies, religion, and philosophy at Oxford and earned his PhD at Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. He held professorships at the University of Chicago, Notre Dame, University of Illinois Chicago, and Duke University.
Paul K. Nietupski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at Columbia University and held an appointment at John Carroll University (attested 2008).

Paul Kingsbury worked in linguistics and Indology, earning his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona. He later served as a program manager at USC and CHOP, and worked in biomedical informatics at the Mayo Clinic.
Paul Kiparsky is a linguist and Indologist who studied at MIT under Morris Halle (~1962–1965). He spent the bulk of his academic career on the faculty at Stanford University from around 1984 to 2020.

Paul Kretschmer was a linguist who earned his PhD at Berlin under Johannes Schmidt and Hermann Diels. He lectured at Berlin and held professorships at the University of Marburg (1897–1899) and the University of Vienna (1899–1936).

Paul L. Swanson, a specialist in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studied at Otani University and earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. He later served as a professor at Nanzan University (attested 1991–2009).
Paul Marriot Wynch was an Indology scholar who joined the Bengal Civil Service in 1808 and studied at the East India Company College from 1809 to 1810.

Paul Masson-Oursel specialized in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, studying under Lévi, Foucher, Bergson, Durkheim, Mauss, and Chavannes. From 1919 he taught at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, serving as directeur d’études from 1927 to 1953.

Paul McBain is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned an MA at the University of Chicago and a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania before becoming a lecturer at Thammasat University in 2021.

Paul Mendes-Flohr was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Brooklyn College and Brandeis University. He served as a director at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and as a professor at the University of Chicago.

Paul Michael Toomey worked in Indology and religious studies, earning his degrees from Bowdoin College and the University of Virginia (PhD). He was associated with the American Institute of Indian Studies and later taught at Cornell University.

Paul Mus specialized in Buddhist studies, religion, and history, studying under Sylvain Lévi and others in Paris. He held major posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, the Collège de France (1946–1969), and Yale University.

Paul Olaf Bodding was a linguist and Indologist who studied theology at the University of Oslo. He was a member of The Asiatic Society and served as head of the Santal Mission of the Northern Churches from 1910 to 1933.

Paul Oltramare worked in Indology and religious studies, studying at Geneva, Basel, and Paris under Paul Deussen and Michel Bréal. He served as professor of Latin at Collège Calvin and professor of the history of religions at Geneva.
Paul Passy was a linguist who studied under Ferdinand de Saussure. He held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from approximately 1894 to 1913.

Paul Pelliot specialized in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology, studying under Sylvain Lévi and Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at the EFEO and as chair of Central Asian languages and history at the Collège de France.

Paul R. Brass was an Indologist who studied at Harvard College, Harvard University, and the University of Chicago. He spent his academic career at the University of Washington from circa 1967 to 2001.

Paul Regnaud was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Abel Bergaigne and Eugène-Armand Hauvette-Besnault, earning degrees at the EPHE and the University of Paris. He taught at the University of Lyon, holding the Sanskrit chair from 1887 to 1908.
